      "title": "API key in the URL query string leaks through logs, proxies and browser history",

      "requirement": {
        "title": "Accept API credentials only in a request header, never in the URL",
        "given": "a partner calls the public REST API",
        "when": "the credential is supplied in the query string",
        "then": "the request is rejected and the key is only accepted in an Authorization header, so credentials never appear in URLs or logs"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Keys never expire, so one stolen key gives permanent partner impersonation",
      "scenario": "A key that leaked years ago from a log, an old integration, a departed partner employee's laptop or a public repository still authenticates today.         "then": "all subsequent requests with that key are rejected, and partners can self-rotate to a new key without downtime"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "One key unlocks every order and every customer email for the partner",
      "scenario": "Each key is all-or-nothing: whoever holds it can read the complete order history and all customer email addresses for that partner.         "then": "the request is denied, and keys can be issued without access to customer email addresses"
      }
    },

      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Order lookups may not check that the order belongs to the calling partner",

      "component": "Orders endpoint object-level authorization",

        { "quote": "Keys never expire and grant access to all of the partner’s orders and customer email addresses." }

      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "A partner might be able to ask for another partner's order by changing the id in the request.",

        "title": "Enforce per-record ownership on every order lookup",
        "given": "an authenticated partner key",
        "when": "a request references an order that belongs to a different partner",
        "then": "the API returns not-found or forbidden and never discloses the record or its customer data"
      }
    },

      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Unthrottled public endpoints allow bulk scraping of customer email addresses",
      "scenario": "Because the API is public and has no rate limiting, a single valid or leaked key can be driven at full speed to walk the whole order history and harvest every customer email address in minutes.       "component": "Public REST API edge",

      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "There is no rate limiting yet." },
        { "quote": "Partners call our public REST API with an API key in the query string." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770", "CWE-307"],
      "plainLanguage": "With no limit on how fast someone can call the API, they can download all the customer emails or guess keys at speed.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Throttle per key and per source, and cap bulk reads",
        "given": "the public REST API",
        "when": "a caller exceeds the configured request or record-volume budget, or repeatedly presents invalid keys",
        "then": "further requests are rejected and the caller is temporarily blocked"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Anyone on the internet can exhaust API capacity with unlimited requests",
      "scenario": "The endpoint is internet-facing with no request limits, so an attacker, or a buggy partner script, can flood it with expensive order queries and exhaust application and database capacity. All partners lose service, and the cost of serving the traffic falls on us.",
      "component": "Public REST API availability",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "There is no rate limiting yet." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-400"],
      "plainLanguage": "Without limits, one noisy or hostile caller can overload the API and take it down for every partner.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Protect availability with quotas and load shedding",
        "given": "sustained high request volume from one or more callers",
        "when": "the configured quota or concurrency limit is reached",
        "then": "excess requests are shed with 429 responses while other partners continue to be served"
      }
    },

      "component": "API key identity model",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Keys never expire and grant access to all of the partner’s orders and customer email addresses." }

      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-1244"],

        "when": "an API call is made",
